efd.title: Error, defect and failure
efd.intro: How a human error becomes a defect in a work product and then a failure when the code runs, and why fixing defects is debugging, not testing.

principles.title: The seven testing principles
principles.intro: The seven ISTQB testing principles, from 'testing shows the presence, not the absence of defects' to the absence-of-defects fallacy, and how the exam twists them.

vv.title: Verification vs validation
vv.intro: Verification checks a work product against its specification; validation checks it against user needs. The most common word swap in CTFL answer options.

activities.title: Test activities and the test process
activities.intro: The seven test activities, from planning to completion, what each one produces, and how to tell test analysis (what to test) from test design (how to test).

testware.title: Testware and traceability
testware.intro: The work products each test activity creates, how test basis differs from testware, and why traceability matters for coverage and impact analysis.

independence.title: Independence of testing
independence.intro: The levels of test independence, from the author testing their own work to external testers, with the benefits and drawbacks the exam asks about.

wholeteam.title: Whole-team approach
wholeteam.intro: Why quality is everyone's job in the whole-team approach, how testers work with business and developers, and when it is not the right fit.

sdlc.title: Sequential vs iterative SDLC models
sdlc.intro: How testing differs in sequential, iterative and incremental lifecycles, and the good testing practices that apply to every SDLC.

levels.title: The five test levels
levels.intro: Component, component integration, system, system integration and acceptance testing: the objective, test basis and typical defects of each level.

leveltype.title: Test levels vs test types
leveltype.intro: Test levels say when testing happens; test types say what it targets. Functional, non-functional, black-box and white-box testing can run at any level.

confreg.title: Confirmation vs regression testing
confreg.intro: Confirmation testing checks that a fix works; regression testing checks that the change broke nothing else. Why regression suites are prime automation candidates.

maint.title: Maintenance testing
maint.intro: Testing changes to a system in operation: triggers such as modification, migration and retirement, and how impact analysis sets the scope.

testfirst.title: Test-first approaches: TDD, ATDD and BDD
testfirst.intro: How test-driven, acceptance test-driven and behavior-driven development differ, who writes the tests and what format each one uses.

shiftleft.title: Shift-left testing
shiftleft.intro: What shift left means in practice, from reviewing requirements to continuous integration, and the trade-off of extra early effort.

staticdyn.title: Static vs dynamic testing
staticdyn.intro: Static testing examines work products without running them and finds defects directly; dynamic testing runs the software and finds failures.

reviews.title: The four review types
reviews.intro: Informal review, walkthrough, technical review and inspection: who leads each one, their objectives and the review roles.

success.title: Review success factors
success.intro: What makes reviews work: clear objectives, the right review type, small chunks, enough time, training and a culture that critiques the product, not the person.

techcat.title: Black-box, white-box and experience-based techniques
techcat.intro: The three families of test techniques in CTFL v4.0.1, what each one is based on and which kinds of defects they find.

ep.title: Equivalence partitioning
ep.intro: Split inputs into partitions processed the same way and test one value from each. Valid and invalid partitions and Each Choice coverage, with exam examples.

bva.title: Boundary value analysis
bva.intro: Test the edges of ordered partitions. 2-value vs 3-value BVA, how to count coverage items and the off-by-one traps in exam questions.

dt.title: Decision table testing
dt.intro: Model combinations of conditions and actions, where each column is a rule. How many columns a full table has and how to minimise it.

st.title: State transition testing
st.intro: Model states, events and transitions. All-states, valid-transitions and all-transitions coverage, and how to count test cases from a diagram.

whitebox.title: Statement and branch coverage
whitebox.intro: White-box testing in CTFL: why 100% branch coverage includes 100% statement coverage but not the other way round.

experience.title: Error guessing, exploratory and checklist-based testing
experience.intro: The three experience-based techniques, when each one shines, and what a test charter is in session-based exploratory testing.

atdd.title: User stories, INVEST and acceptance criteria
atdd.intro: Collaborative user story writing, the 3 Cs, the INVEST criteria and how acceptance criteria drive ATDD test cases.

plan.title: The test plan
plan.intro: What a test plan contains, why writing it helps, and how entry and exit criteria (Definition of Ready and Done) fit in.

relplan.title: Release vs iteration planning
relplan.intro: What testers contribute to release planning and to iteration planning in iterative development.

estimate.title: Test estimation and three-point estimation
estimate.intro: Ratio-based, extrapolation, Wideband Delphi and three-point estimation, with the (a + 4m + b) / 6 formula worked through.

prio.title: Test case prioritization
prio.intro: Risk-based, coverage-based and requirements-based prioritization, and why dependencies can change the execution order.

pyrquad.title: Test pyramid vs testing quadrants
pyrquad.intro: The test pyramid sorts tests by granularity; the testing quadrants sort them by purpose. Which tests go in Q1 to Q4.

risk.title: Risk and risk-based testing
risk.intro: Risk level = likelihood × impact. Product vs project risk, risk analysis and risk control, and how risk shapes testing.

config.title: Configuration management vs defect management
config.intro: Configuration management versions and tracks testware and test items; defect management runs the lifecycle of each defect.

defect.title: The defect report
defect.intro: What a good defect report contains, and the difference between severity and priority that the exam loves to test.

reports.title: Test progress vs test completion report
reports.intro: What goes into a test progress report during testing and into a test completion report at the end, and who reads them.

tooltypes.title: Types of test tools
tooltypes.intro: Management, static testing, test design, execution and coverage, non-functional, DevOps and collaboration tools: how to classify a tool in an exam question.

automation.title: Test automation: benefits and risks
automation.intro: What test automation really saves, the risks of unrealistic expectations and tool dependence, and how to introduce a tool.
